title: Phase 9 · Stage 26: Creating books and members
summary: Accept JSON request DTOs, validate every field into a ValidationProblem, and answer 201 Created, 400 or 409.

steps.title: DTOs at the edge
body: Writing to the API means accepting **JSON from strangers**. Never bind it straight onto domain objects: a `Book` with a private setter and guard clauses is exactly what you do not want a JSON parser poking at. Instead, each endpoint takes a **request DTO**, a record made for the wire, where everything is **nullable** because anything may be missing:
record CreateBookRequest(string? Isbn, string? Title, string? Author, int? Year, int? Copies, string? Genre);
var errors = Validation.ForBook(request, out Genre genre);        // every problem, not just the first
`Results.ValidationProblem` answers **400** with the standard *problem details* JSON (`application/problem+json`), one list of messages per field:
{"title":"One or more validation errors occurred.","status":400,"errors":{"title":["Title is required."],"year":["Year must be from 1450 to 2026."]}}

Validation answers *is this request well-formed?* The domain still answers *is it allowed?*: a duplicate ISBN passes validation, then `library.AddBook` returns a `Conflict` result, which becomes **409**.

steps.prompt: Which status code should each request get?
items: a new book with every field valid
a book whose ISBN is already in the catalog
a member whose email is already registered
steps.explain: 400 means *fix your request*; 409 means *the request is fine, but it clashes with what the server already has*.

steps.prompt: Why is `Year` an `int?` in `CreateBookRequest` rather than an `int`?
options: So a missing year arrives as null and can be reported, instead of silently becoming 0
Because the domain stores years as nullable
steps.explain: With `int`, a request without a year would bind to 0 and fail with a confusing range message, or worse, pass a check written as `>= 0`.
A relational pattern never matches null, so `is not (...)` is true for a missing year as well as for one out of range: one check covers both.

steps.title: POST /books
prompt: - `record CreateBookRequest(string? Isbn, string? Title, string? Author, int? Year, int? Copies, string? Genre)`
- `static class Validation` with `Dictionary<string, string[]> ForBook(CreateBookRequest request, out Genre genre)` and `Genre? ParseGenre(string text)` (any case).
| isbn, title, author missing or blank | `isbn`: `ISBN is required.` / `title`: `Title is required.` / `author`: `Author is required.` |
| year missing or outside 1450..2026 | `year`: `Year must be from 1450 to 2026.` |
| copies missing or below 1 | `copies`: `Copies must be at least 1.` |
| genre given but unknown | `genre`: `Genre must be one of General, Fiction, Mystery, Science, History, Children.` |

`POST /books`: any errors → **400** `ValidationProblem`. Otherwise build the `Book` (trimmed text; no genre means General) and `library.AddBook` it: a failure is **409** `Results.Problem(detail: result.Error, statusCode: 409)`; success is **201** with `Location: /books/{isbn}` and the `BookDto`.

static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("creating a book could be checked", async () =>
var r = await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/books", new { isbn = " 978-0618640157 ", title = "The Lord of the Rings", author = "J.R.R. Tolkien", year = 1954, copies = 2, genre = "fiction" });
DojoWeb.Status("POST /books with a good book responds 201 Created", 201, r);
var location = r.Headers.Location?.ToString() ?? "";
Dojo.Check("with Location: /books/978-0618640157", location.EndsWith("/books/978-0618640157"), "the Location header was " + (location == "" ? "missing" : location));
var json = await DojoWeb.Json(r);
Dojo.Eq("the body is the new book, ISBN trimmed", "978-0618640157", DojoWeb.Prop(json, "isbn"));
Dojo.Eq("its genre is Fiction", "Fiction", DojoWeb.Prop(json, "genre"));
Dojo.Eq("GET /books/978-0618640157 now finds it", "The Lord of the Rings", DojoWeb.Prop(await GetJson(http, "/books/978-0618640157"), "title"));
Dojo.Eq("GET /books lists it last", "978-0261103344,978-0441172719,978-0141439518,978-0618640157", Keys(await GetJson(http, "/books"), "isbn"));
var plain = await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/books", new { isbn = "978-0000000001", title = "Plain", author = "A. Writer", year = 2000, copies = 1 });
Dojo.Eq("a book without a genre is General", "General", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(plain), "genre"));
await Dojo.TryAsync("validation could be checked", async () =>
var r = await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/books", new { isbn = "", author = "  ", year = 1200, copies = 0, genre = "Poetry" });
DojoWeb.Status("POST /books with bad fields responds 400 Bad Request", 400, r);
Dojo.Check("as application/problem+json", IsProblem(r), "the content type was " + r.Content.Headers.ContentType);
var errors = Get(await DojoWeb.Json(r), "errors");
Dojo.Eq("errors.isbn explains the ISBN", "ISBN is required.", First(errors, "isbn"));
Dojo.Eq("errors.title explains the title", "Title is required.", First(errors, "title"));
Dojo.Eq("errors.author explains the author", "Author is required.", First(errors, "author"));
Dojo.Eq("errors.year explains the year", "Year must be from 1450 to 2026.", First(errors, "year"));
Dojo.Eq("errors.copies explains the copies", "Copies must be at least 1.", First(errors, "copies"));
Dojo.Eq("errors.genre lists the genres", "Genre must be one of General, Fiction, Mystery, Science, History, Children.", First(errors, "genre"));

static string Keys(JsonElement json, string property) => json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array
? string.Join(",", json.EnumerateArray().Select(e => DojoWeb.Prop(e, property)))
: "(not a JSON array: " + json.ValueKind + ")";
static JsonElement At(JsonElement json, int index) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && index < json.GetArrayLength() ? json[index] : default;
static JsonElement Get(JsonElement json, string property) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object && json.TryGetProperty(property, out var value) ? value : default;
static async Task<JsonElement> GetJson(HttpClient http, string url) => await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync(url));
static bool IsProblem(HttpResponseMessage r) => r.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType == "application/problem+json";
static string? First(JsonElement errors, string key) { var list = Get(errors, key); return list.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && list.GetArrayLength() > 0 ? list[0].GetString() : null; }

// "a,b,c" from one property of every item in a JSON array, so one row checks which items came back, in order.
static string Keys(JsonElement json, string property) => json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array
? string.Join(",", json.EnumerateArray().Select(e => DojoWeb.Prop(e, property)))
: "(not a JSON array: " + json.ValueKind + ")";
static JsonElement At(JsonElement json, int index) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && index < json.GetArrayLength() ? json[index] : default;
static JsonElement Get(JsonElement json, string property) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object && json.TryGetProperty(property, out var value) ? value : default;
static async Task<JsonElement> GetJson(HttpClient http, string url) => await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync(url));
static bool IsProblem(HttpResponseMessage r) => r.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType == "application/problem+json";
static string? First(JsonElement errors, string key) { var list = Get(errors, key); return list.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && list.GetArrayLength() > 0 ? list[0].GetString() : null; }
